newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat discusses Hebron with U.S. envoy Ross.
newsitem.headline: Arafat discusses Hebron with U.S. envoy Ross.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross on Friday to discuss obstacles to a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Neither man would say after the talks in Gaza whether Israel and the Palestinians were close to clinching an agreement on Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live in enclaves among 100,000 Arabs.
"We hope to see a final agreement as soon as possible," Ross told reporters. "I think we really exhaustively went into the issues where we're really trying to work together to overcome differences."

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to clinch a Hebron deal in nearly three weeks of U.S.-brokered talks. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said this week an agreement was close but accused Arafat of procrastinating.
Arafat rejected Netanyahu's charge. "He should remember that I am the one who will sign this agreement," he told reporters after meeting Ross.
He summoned a meeting of his cabinet later to discuss the situation ahead of the scheduled resumption of talks with Israel on Saturday night.

Palestinians regard the Hebron redeployment as a litmus test showing whether right-winger Netanyahu will honour peace deals reached with the centre-left Israeli government which he ousted in elections in May.

Israel initially postponed the the pullback because of Islamic militant suicide bombings in Israel in February and March and Netanyahu now says the agreement should be modified to safeguard Hebron's Jewish settlers.
